title: Bijectivity of canonical homology evaluation
statement: Let k be any commutative ring and choose the derived category of ModuleCat k [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor]. For every derived object A and every integer n, the explicitly constructed k-linear map cupHomologyEvaluation [def-sc-module-cup-homology-evaluation] from Hom(Q(S(n)),A) to H^n(A) is bijective.

source.place: Lemma 13.19.8, followed by evaluation of a single-complex chain map and its homotopy on 1

proof.text: For a projective P and E with E.IsLE (n-1), choose the strictly bounded-above representative supplied by DerivedCategory.exists_iso_Q_obj_of_isLE. Apply Mathlib DerivedCategory.from_singleFunctor_obj_eq_zero_of_projective and cancel the representative isomorphism. This is the completely proved private helper projective_single_to_lower_eq_zero.

Use the canonical distinguished triangle T = τ<n(A) → A → τ≥n(A). T.obj₁ has homology at most n-1; its shift by 1 has homology at most n-2, hence at most n-1. The first helper makes maps from P[-n] to both objects zero. The exact Hom sequence (T.coyoneda_exact₂ and T.coyoneda_exact₃) then makes postcomposition with T.mor₂ bijective. The source-library DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor_map_bijective_of_isLE_of_isGE n makes H^n bijective on maps P[-n] → T.obj₃. DerivedCategory.isIso_homologyFunctor_map_truncGEπ_app makes H^n(T.mor₂) an isomorphism. Use functoriality and cancellation in this square to prove the fully proved private helper projective_single_homology_bijective for arbitrary n and A.

Set P=ModuleCat.of k k, which is projective. Compose the bijective homology map with Iso.homCongr for ε = homologyFunctorFactors.app S followed by singleObjHomologySelfIso, then with ModuleCat.homAddEquiv and LinearMap.ringLmapEquivSelf k ℤ. This gives the bijective map f ↦ (ε.inv ≫ H^n(f))(1). Unfolding ε and cupHomologyEvaluation proves that it is exactly the specified evaluation map. No arbitrary equivalence is selected; all degrees, the zero ring and unbounded A are included.
